*Packages to load*

```{r}
library(e1071)
library(caret)
```

**1. Data Pre-Processing and Missingness Analysis**

Firstly we import the test and training data that was left after the EDA:

```{r}
train_data<-read.csv("../processed-data/football_train_data.csv")
test_data<-read.csv("../processed-data/football_test_data.csv")
```

Finding the number of rows:

```{r}
nrow(train_data)
nrow(test_data)
```

Now we check which predictors have no missing variables:

```{r}
# Pulling out the predictor variables from the outcome
predictors<-setdiff(names(train_data), "FTR")

selected_predictors <- predictors[
    colSums(is.na(train_data[, predictors, drop = FALSE])) == 0
]

selected_predictors
```

This means that all predictors have at least one row with missing values, which is a problem.
It seems odd for the simple match statistics to have missing values - let's just check the extent of it:

```{r}
# Seeing which rows have missing values of Away Shots on Target
which(is.na(train_data$AST))
```

After personally inspecting the Excel file, this row seems to have N/A for all of the match statistics.
Removing it and inspecting for missingness:

```{r}
train_data1<-train_data[-8808,]
sum(colSums(is.na(train_data1[, predictors, drop = FALSE])) == 0)
```

Now 10 predictors have no missing values - slightly lower than expected of 12 match statistics.
Looking at which were fine:

```{r}
selected_predictors1 <- predictors[
    colSums(is.na(train_data1[, predictors, drop = FALSE])) == 0
]
selected_predictors1
```

AF and HF are the only two match statistics missing. Investigating:

```{r}
which(is.na(train_data$AF))
which(is.na(train_data$HF))
```

So now for a NON-Betting Model we can use the training data without these 3 rows: (for now we aren't going to do any imputation as it isn't strictly necessary when we still have 37821 observations)

```{r}
train_data_NB<-train_data[-c(8808,32940,32949),]
selected_predictors_NB<- predictors[
    colSums(is.na(train_data_NB[, predictors, drop = FALSE])) == 0
]
```

Just checking again that this works:

```{r}
sum(colSums(is.na(train_data_NB[, predictors, drop = FALSE])) == 0)
selected_predictors_NB
nrow(train_data_NB)
```

Next we will further examine missingness in order to get a training dataset that we can use for a Betting Odds Model:

```{r}
# We've already checked for the (non-betting) match statistics
odds_var<-setdiff(names(train_data), selected_predictors_NB)

missingness <- data.frame(
  Variable = odds_var,
  Missing_N = sapply(train_data[odds_var], function(x) sum(is.na(x))),
  Missing_Percent = sapply(
    train_data[odds_var],
    function(x) mean(is.na(x)) * 100
  )
)

missingness <- missingness[
  order(-missingness$Missing_Percent),
]
```

Checking the table:

```{r}
missingness
```

Unfortunately it seems that a vast majority of the values for the betting odds are missing. However the Bet365 variables (for Home win, Draw, Away win) have only 0.024% missingness. Investigating where:

```{r}
which(is.na(train_data$B365A))
which(is.na(train_data$B365D))
which(is.na(train_data$B365H))
```

So only 9 more rows with missing values (none overlapping with the match statistics). For the Betting Model we will use the training data without these rows as well as the previous 3 rows we found:

```{r}
train_data_B<-train_data_NB[complete.cases(train_data_NB[, c("B365H", "B365D", "B365A")]),]
selected_predictors_B<-unique(c(selected_predictors_NB, "B365H", "B365D", "B365A"))
nrow(train_data_B)
```

Again for now we are fine to use this as training data without imputation, but we will do imputation later.

**2. Fitting the Baseline SVM models**

Now we can train an SVM for each training dataset. First the Non-Betting model:

```{r}
# First converting the result to a factor variable
train_data_NB$FTR<-factor(train_data_NB$FTR, levels=c("H", "D", "A"))

# Fitting with default values of the parameters
baseline_svm_model_NB<-svm(FTR~., data=train_data_NB[, c("FTR", selected_predictors_NB)],
               kernel="radial", cost=1, gamma=1/length(selected_predictors_NB), scale=TRUE)
```

and the Betting model:

```{r}
train_data_B$FTR<-factor(train_data_B$FTR, levels=c("H", "D", "A"))
baseline_svm_model_B<-svm(FTR~., data=train_data_B[, c("FTR", selected_predictors_B)],
                 kernel="radial", cost=1, gamma=1/length(selected_predictors_B), scale=TRUE)
```

For a preliminary check, we can look at metrics such as the confusion matrix, accuracy, precision ,recall, F1 score etc. on the training sets of each. First defining a function that can do this:

```{r}
calculate_metrics <- function(actual, predicted) {

  actual <- factor(actual, levels = c("H", "D", "A"))
  predicted <- factor(predicted, levels = c("H", "D", "A"))

  cm <- confusionMatrix(
    data = predicted,
    reference = actual
  )

  tab <- cm$table

  precision <- diag(tab) / rowSums(tab)
  recall <- diag(tab) / colSums(tab)

  f1 <- 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)

  overall <- data.frame(
    Accuracy = as.numeric(cm$overall["Accuracy"]),
    Kappa = as.numeric(cm$overall["Kappa"]),
    Macro_Precision = mean(precision, na.rm = TRUE),
    Macro_Recall = mean(recall, na.rm = TRUE),
    Macro_F1 = mean(f1, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

  by_class <- data.frame(
    Outcome = c("Home win", "Draw", "Away win"),
    Precision = as.numeric(precision),
    Recall = as.numeric(recall),
    F1 = as.numeric(f1)
  )

  list(
    confusion_matrix = tab,
    overall = overall,
    by_class = by_class
  )
}
```

and then making predictions using the training datasets:

```{r}
baseline_training_predictions_NB<-predict(baseline_svm_model_NB, newdata=train_data_NB[, selected_predictors_NB, drop=FALSE])
baseline_training_predictions_B<-predict(baseline_svm_model_B, newdata=train_data_B[, selected_predictors_B, drop=FALSE])
```

Now we can view the performance metrics of this preliminary check:

```{r}
baseline_training_metrics_NB<-calculate_metrics(actual=train_data_NB$FTR,
                                                predicted = baseline_training_predictions_NB)
baseline_training_metrics_B<-calculate_metrics(actual=train_data_B$FTR,
                                               predicted = baseline_training_predictions_B)
```

First let's see the training performance of the Non-Betting model:

```{r}
baseline_training_metrics_NB$overall
```
```{r}
baseline_training_metrics_NB$by_class
```
```{r}
baseline_training_metrics_NB$confusion_matrix
```

and now the Betting model:

```{r}
baseline_training_metrics_B$overall
```
```{r}
baseline_training_metrics_B$by_class
```
```{r}
baseline_training_metrics_B$confusion_matrix
```
